Runs a tile in a cloned process, with argument parsing, CPU affinity, and optional pipe PID output.

# Purpose
`run1.c` implements a command handler that starts one topology tile in a separate cloned process. It parses the command line in [`run1_cmd_args`](<#run1_cmd_args>), reads the tile name and kind ID, and can also accept a `--pipe-fd` option used to return the child PID to the caller. The file then finds the matching tile in `config->topo`, sets the thread and log state for the new execution context, selects a CPU for the tile, and prepares the tile stack with `fd_topo_tile_stack_join`.

The main execution path is in [`run1_cmd_fn`](<#run1_cmd_fn>), which uses `clone()` to run [`tile_main`](<#tile_main>) for the selected tile. [`tile_main`](<#tile_main>) builds a `fd_topo_run_tile_t` object with `fdctl_tile_run()` and enters `fd_topo_run_tile()`, which runs the tile loop with the current topology, sandbox, core dump, user ID, group ID, and optional debug synchronization. The file also supports sandbox mode with `CLONE_NEWPID`, so the tile can run in its own PID namespace and cannot signal other processes in the parent tree.
